items.title: Live: Israel yet to respond as US touts disarmament deal with Hamas
items.description: US President Donald Trump says a deal has been reached for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its forces from Gaza. Follow live.

items.title: 'No good alternative': US burns through expensive missiles fighting Iran
items.description: The cost of the US war in Iran continues to skyrocket with vast amounts of expensive high-end missile interceptors being used to defend against waves of cheap Iranian drones and ballistic missiles.

items.title: The 'little shampoo business' selling 'false hope' to women
items.description: Sellers for a multi-level marketing company promise sisterhood, success and a more flexible life. But former insiders say that, for most, the reality is far from what is being sold on social media.

items.title: Anthropic's Claude AI model hacks three companies during safety tests
items.description: The admission from Anthropic comes just days after ‌rival company OpenAI revealed a rogue agent had gone on a days-long ‌hacking spree at ⁠AI firm Hugging Face.

items.title: Australian rock music journalist Glenn A Baker dies
items.description: Baker has been remembered by his family as "somebody who absolutely grabbed life" and found "joy" in music after an unsettled childhood.

items.title: Live: Warning small business will be hit with 'massive tax increases' under trust changes
items.description: The Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry has trashed the government's proposal for a minimum 30 per cent tax on discretionary trusts. Follow live.

items.title: Record-smashing El Niño points to spring of drought and fires
items.description: Despite El Niño being months away from peaking, it could potentially trigger Australia's hottest spring on record.

items.title: Luke Gosling facing growing calls to stand down after assault charges
items.description: Labor's political opponents have lined up to call for the prime minister to force Solomon MP Luke Gosling to stand aside from his special envoy role after he was charged with assaulting the NT administrator.

items.title: Spain deploys military after thousands breach its North Africa border
items.description: Thousands of migrants have been reported to have made the crossing earlier this week, some by water, leading to the Spain deploying troops to the border.

items.title: Social media pushing young adults towards 'DIY dentistry'
items.description: Young Australians are living with untreated dental issues as they’re also bombarded with dubious social media advice.

items.title: Parents of Australian facing possible death penalty in Syria question confession
items.description: The family of a Gold Coast man who has been charged with murder over the death of an Australian in Syria is frustrated by the lack of progress made by the federal government in the case.

items.title: Shipwreck cargo reveals 400-year-old global trade secrets
items.description: An analysis of cargo from one of Australia's best-known shipwrecks uncovers complex global trade routes from nearly 400 years ago.

items.title: 'Never for sale': European nations vow World Cup boycott over FIFA plan
items.description: FIFA boss Gianni Infantino's controversial plan to sell 20 per cent of the organisation's commercial operations to private investors hits trouble, with European nations threatening a World Cup boycott if it goes ahead.

items.title: Live: US stocks lift and ASX 200 set to follow
items.description: US stocks lifted, and the ASX 200 is set to follow despite fresh conflict in the Middle East. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Friday news quiz: Neil the seal's damage bill, unusual birthing methods and three premiers in one day
items.description: You too could find yourself named interim premier of Victoria if you can hold your own in today's news quiz.

items.title: The Strokes, Charli XCX, Jack White: who had the best album of July?
items.description: Blockbuster acts might have grabbed music headlines but it was Australian artists that had some of the best new releases of the month.

items.title: From bedrotting to erotic art by Lucy Liu, these artists talk about being lonely
items.description: So many people around the world are lonely. But how do you capture the feeling? A new exhibition brings together 11 artists, including Lucy Liu, to make you less lonely.

items.title: Quick hits: Tongan dance moves bring joy, David Beckham hits the velodrome
items.description: David Beckham and Ronaldo get on their bikes at the velodrome, a para athletics race will be run again amid much drama, and a Tongan weightlifter thrills the crowd with his dancing. Here are the quick hits from day seven of the Commonwealth Games.

items.title: 'It was weird': De Minaur beats Hewitt in Aussie tussle
items.description: World number six Alex de Minaur puts the brakes on Cruz Hewitt's rapid rise to keep his title defence alive in Washington and race into the quarter-finals.

items.title: Meet the man dressed as a bin who is trying to disrupt British politics
items.description: A novelty candidate called Count Binface will next month try to unseat one of the most prominent politicians in the United Kingdom when constituents in Clacton-on-Sea head to the polls.

items.title: Melbourne Uni confronts complex legacy as Aboriginal remains repatriated
items.description: Decades after being taken by a University of Melbourne anthropologist, the remains of nine Aboriginal ancestors have been returned to their sacred home in Arnhem Land.

items.title: Albanese's absence looms large over Garma
items.description: The theme of this year's Garma Festival is "bukmak", a Yolŋu word meaning "everyone", but the prime minister's decision not to attend may indicate how high on the government's priority list Indigenous affairs sit.

items.title: Expeditioners given 'substandard' clothing, leaking tents on sub-Antarctic island
items.description: The Australian Antarctic Division says there are "lessons to be learnt" after expeditioners were issued with "substandard" clothing and leaking tents on an island about 4,000 kilometres south-west of the Australian mainland.

items.title: Chargeback fraud cripples businesses as banks fail to take responsibility
items.description: Despite evidence proving a customer accidentally lodged a chargeback, the bank denied the dispute from a small business owner. It raises the question of what protections are in place for this modern type of fraud.

items.title: Woman sues for pregnancy discrimination and wins in rare case
items.description: Research shows pregnant women and new mothers are routinely let go from their jobs, discriminated against, and, in one case, forced to pump breastmilk in a storeroom. We want to hear your stories.
